title: A Survival Factor Has a Ceiling

scenes.tts: Give a young mammal extra nerve growth factor, and its sympathetic ganglia swell. Inject a newborn mouse with an antiserum against it, and the ganglia waste away. Call the protein N G F. Results like these tempt a strong conclusion. Does N G F decide how many neurons an animal has?
scenes.caption: Give a young mammal extra nerve growth factor, and its sympathetic ganglia swell. Inject a newborn mouse with an antiserum against it, and the ganglia waste away. Call the protein NGF. Results like these tempt a strong conclusion. Does NGF decide how many neurons an animal has?
scenes.visual: A ganglion of dots swells when a yellow NGF chip arrives, shrinks and reddens under an antiserum chip, then returns to normal under a large question mark.
scenes.narration: Give a young mammal extra nerve growth factor, and its sympathetic ganglia swell. Inject a newborn mouse with an antiserum against it, and the ganglia waste away. Call the protein NGF. Results like these tempt a strong conclusion. Does NGF decide how many neurons an animal has?

scenes.tts: A small ganglion can mean two things. Either too few neurons were made, or the normal number was made and some were lost. In chick spinal ganglia, many neurons formed and grew fibres first. Dying cells became conspicuous later. Neurons are overproduced.
scenes.visual: Two panels end on the same small ganglion, one never filled, one filled then emptied. Then a timeline: neurons appear, later some turn red and fade.
scenes.narration: A small ganglion can mean two things. Either too few neurons were made, or the normal number was made and some were lost. In chick spinal ganglia, many neurons formed and grew fibres first. Dying cells became conspicuous later. Neurons are overproduced.

scenes.tts: The target is the tissue an axon grows to and connects with. It supplies the factor, and the amount is limited. Axons that reach the target take it up. Neurons that get too little die by apoptosis. The idea is that neurons compete for a limiting amount of factor. Death should come when axons reach the target, not before.
scenes.visual: Twelve neurons send axons to a target holding a few yellow factor dots. Neurons that take one turn green; the rest turn red and fade.
scenes.narration: The target is the tissue an axon grows to and connects with. It supplies the factor, and the amount is limited. Axons that reach the target take it up. scenes.tts: An antiserum carries a doubt. It might kill neurons by binding something other than N G F. A knockout mouse settles it. Mice lacking a working T R K A, the receptor for N G F, still form the ganglion. Neurons are made and their axons start to grow as usual. But the sympathetic neurons are lost after embryonic day fifteen point five. The neurons were produced. What failed was survival.

scenes.visual: A crossed-out TrkA chip; a schematic count of neurons in the ganglion rises to the number made, then falls after a marked day; the fall is labelled survival.

scenes.tts: Now add excess N G F to a developing chick embryo. The ganglia get larger, because more of the neurons that were made escape the normal death. How would you know it is survival? You count neurons and dying cells across the death period, and you mark dividing cells. No new neurons appear from nothing, and no neuron changes what kind of neuron it is.

scenes.visual: The target is flooded with yellow factor; the red ghost neurons turn green again; an empty extra slot above the column stays empty.

scenes.tts: This gives a ceiling. Neurons surviving equal the smaller of two numbers: the neurons made, and the neurons the factor can support. Extra factor raises the second number. Nothing about a survival factor raises the first. The ceiling holds for the population you measured, with its own factor. A survival factor can decide how many of the neurons made stay alive. It cannot add neurons that were never made.
scenes.visual: A plot of survivors against factor supply rises, then flattens at a dashed line for neurons made; a marker slides along it.
